aspects.says: An effectively immutable object is correct after one safe publication with no locks on reads, but not through a racy reference.
basis: section:Immutable Objects Need No Edge; Effectively Immutable Ones Need One Safe Publication

aspects.says: A constructor that hands out this, even on its last line, lets others see a subclass's final fields at their defaults and loses the final-field guarantee; build first, then register or start.
basis: section:A Constructor That Lets this Escape Hands Out an Object Before It Is Built
section:Spot the Problem: Registered on the Last Line

aspects.says: A thread that sees an object after its constructor finished is guaranteed its final fields, and what they reach as of that moment, even through a race; plain fields of the same object get no guarantee.
basis: section:final Fields Are Guaranteed Through a Race, and Nothing Else in the Object Is

aspects.says: An object is immutable only if nothing it reaches can change after construction: a record keeping a caller's list, or an unmodifiable view of it, changes when the caller's list does, and nested collections need copies too.
basis: section:Immutable Objects Need No Edge; Effectively Immutable Ones Need One Safe Publication

aspects.says: A reference written with no happens-before edge may reach a reader before the writes that built the object, though the reference write itself is atomic; a run that never shows it proves nothing.
basis: section:A Reference Written Without an Edge Can Arrive Before the Writes That Built the Object

aspects.says: Safe publication is a release by the writer after building the object and the matching acquire by the reader: a volatile or AtomicReference field, one lock on both sides, a concurrent collection, a static initializer; it covers the writes made before the release.
basis: section:Safe Publication Is an Edge From the Object's Construction to the Read of Its Reference

aspects.says: A static initializer publishes to every thread that uses the class, and one that throws leaves the class failed: NoClassDefFoundError on every later use until restart.
basis: section:A Static Initializer Publishes to Every Thread, and Fails for Every Thread

aspects.says: javac -Xlint:this-escape (Java 21) warns when a constructor can leak this to an external subclass, and is silent when the class is package-private.
aspects.reason: a compiler warning: the graded runner compiles the reader's code with the course's fixed flags and reports test results, not lint output

aspects.says: A thread started in a constructor gets an edge for the writes before start() only, so it may read the fields assigned after it, final ones included, at their defaults.
basis: section:A Constructor That Lets this Escape Hands Out an Object Before It Is Built
